waiting.kind: Sign a correction and a list change
waiting.title: 42078 Mack Anthem: the container's second door has parts the booklet does not give it, and the doors need their lock bars lifted first
waiting.what: Two things, signed together. (1) A correction to the model file. The booklet builds the container's two end doors differently: door 1 gets an 11L beam and a 13L beam on two blue pins (page 409, step 43); door 2 gets black pins, an 11L beam and a 7L beam, and no 13L beam or blue pins (page 415, steps 58 and 59). In the file, door 2 is door 1 mirrored, so it has door 1's 13L beam and blue pins too. That beam lies in the same place as door 1's, and the blue pins run into door 1, so the two doors are tied to each other and neither can swing. The correction takes those three parts out of door 2 and puts in the two black pins that hold its 11L beam. (2) A change to function 12's list. Today it reads: The container's two end doors swing open. New: The container's two end doors swing open, each once its lock bar is lifted. Each door has a lock bar whose pin stands in the container (page 418, step 69). The check now lifts each bar first, then works both doors.
waiting.effect: Function 12 of the 42078 goes from doesn't work to works: one more working function. In the viewer: Shift-press a lock bar and drag it up, then Shift-press the door and drag it. Each door opens about 13 degrees and then meets the rear crane, which stands just in front of the doors while the container is on the trailer.
waiting.confidence: High for the correction: Claude read pages 409, 415 and 418 itself, and they show the two doors built differently. High for the function: the check gives works with both in, and a drag in the viewer lifted each bar 20 LDU and swung the doors 12.7 and 12.8 degrees. One thing to know: the booklet's functions pages (420 and 421) do not show the doors open, so the function's wording is ours, from the building steps.

waiting.kind: Sign two corrections and a list change
waiting.title: 8110 Unimog: the crane's drive shaft is drawn broken in two places, and our list had the wrong lever settings
waiting.what: Three things, signed together. (1) A correction: the universal joint at the gearbox's rear output is drawn as one end only, with no cross and no second end, so the shaft to the crane is joined to nothing. The booklet puts an axle 8 into a whole universal joint there (book 2, page 3, step 65). The correction adds the cross and the second end. (2) A correction: at the shaft's other end, the ball is drawn 6.2 LDU short of the cup it drives (book 2, page 24, step 77). The correction moves it into the cup. (3) A change to our list's lever settings, read from the file and matched to the functions page (book 5, page 43). Red lever down and yellow up: the winch (function 7, unchanged). Both levers up: the crane slews (function 8; our list had the winch's setting here). Yellow lever down: the compressor (function 9; our list moved the red lever instead). Function 10, the page's fourth picture, is the compressor again: the red knob on the side is the lever of a pneumatic valve, so it switches the air, not the drive. Function 6's words change from four outputs to three.
waiting.effect: Function 8 (the crane slews) goes from partly to works. Function 10 goes from works to partly: its works was hollow, because it listed nothing to move, and it now lists the compressor's crank, which stops after a small turn (as function 9 does; the solver owner traces that next). So the count does not change until the compressor is mended.
waiting.confidence: High. Claude read the three booklet pages itself. The worker traced all four lever settings through the gearbox, and each agrees with the functions page. In preview's viewer, with the corrections: both levers dragged up, the motor run for a minute, the turntable's gear turned at the check's rate and the winch stayed still.
